messages:
Maya Patel: quick follow-up to yesterday's RFC thread about the model gatekeeper flow — should we go single-monolith gate or a chain of focused validators? I want pros/cons before I write the follow-up doc.
Samir Gupta: chain of validators. easier to reason about and to reuse across entrypoints (hosted / dedicated / private). downside: more roundtrips and infra surface.
Eli Wang: +1 chain but add short-circuiting. do cheap checks first (artifact schema, signature, tiny smoke bench) and only run heavy evals if those pass. that minimizes cost for obvious failures.
Irene Cole: question: how do we express the compatibility contract for runtimes? we need a stable interface so infra teams can incrementally change runtime adapters without breaking validators.
Samir Gupta: interface suggestion: validators talk to a single "gatekeeper" coordinator which exposes: POST /validate -> returns {status, phase_results[], artifact_id}. coordinator handles sequencing and retries. keep validator plugins stateless.
Eli Wang: sample sequencing I had in mind: 1) artifact manifest + schema check, 2) binary signature & sha, 3) lightweight runtime smoke (load + 1 request), 4) perf micro-bench (p50/p95 latency estimate), 5) eval suite (quality/regression). short-circuit at first failure.
Maya Patel: sounds good. tradeoff: more stages = more surface for failures and harder to debug for model owners. can we surface an ordered trace with links to logs and diffs?
Irene Cole: yes — add trace IDs and attach NJ observability links. also, we should version the manifest contract: inference_manifest_v1, v2, etc. include required fields: model_family, entry_point, ops_compatibility, quantization_hint.
onboard-bot: AUTO: smoke-check v1 for artifact a5f9 completed: PASS (load 0.45s, single-token predict ok). logs -> https://ci.internal/runs/562
Samir Gupta: tradeoffs we debated in RFC: strict hard gates reduce bad rollouts but slow down model iteration. alternative: soft-fail + canary rollout. allow model to be served to <1% traffic on soft-fail with monitoring alerts.
Eli Wang: operationally neat: hard gates for security/format + runtime invariants (e.g., missing KV cache hooks), soft gates for quality regressions unless explicitly blocked by product.
Maya Patel: question for platform: do we want validator plugins deployed per-cluster (local) or centrally (cloud-run)? latency/cost vs security concerns.
Irene Cole: for private deployments we must run validators on-prem. plan: validator code is portable (container) + coordinator orchestrates either local executor or our hosted executor. manifest should include a field "validation_policy": [hosted, onprem, both].
Samir Gupta: long-term refactor idea: break validators into three microservices: "sanity", "compat", "perf". each exposes the same plugin shim. grafting new checks is just adding a new container. migration cost upfront but gives us independent scaling.
Eli Wang: proto for plugin shim (sketch):
```
service ValidatorPlugin {
  rpc RunCheck(CheckRequest) returns (CheckResult);
}
message CheckRequest { string artifact_id = 1; string phase = 2; map<string,string> meta = 3; }
message CheckResult { bool pass = 1; string details_url = 2; repeated string warnings = 3; }
```
This keeps language agnostic and low-latency.
Maya Patel: nice. performance concern: we should add a budget param so heavy evals can be rate/CPU limited: budget_ms or token_limit.
Irene Cole: agree — also add cost-accounting in the trace so teams see estimated $$ consumed by validations. prevents surprise bills.
Samir Gupta: governance: default policy = allow soft-fail canary; hard-fail only for format, signature, ops_compat. allow org override via manifest tag `force_hard_gate`.
Maya Patel: next steps: I'll draft a short RFC addendum proposing chain-of-checks with short-circuit + plugin shim + canary policy. prototype plan: implement coordinator + one plugin (smoke + perf microbench) in 2 weeks. owners: eng-ml (Eli/Samir) + eng-platform (Irene).
Eli Wang: happy to pair on prototype. will sketch coordinator API and a minimal dockerized plugin.
Irene Cole: I'll scope on-prem runner and the manifest versioning doc.
onboard-bot: NOTE: follow-up task created #VAL-214 in backlog, assignees Maya, Eli, Irene.
Maya Patel: ok thanks — I'll push the addendum draft later today and ping for reviews. :thumbsup:
